text: How was the Brooklyn Bridge built? When it opened, it was the longest suspension bridge on Earth.
Work began in eighteen seventy. Its designer, John Roebling, had died, so his son Washington took over.
First, caissons: giant upside-down wooden boxes, sunk into the riverbed, where men dug in compressed air.
Brooklyn's sank forty four feet, Manhattan's seventy eight. Workers got the bends, and Washington was left bedridden.
His wife Emily carried his orders. On the caissons, granite towers rose two hundred seventy six feet.
On shore, anchorages: sixty thousand tons of stone, holding chains for the cables.
From eighteen seventy seven, wheels spun steel wire across the river. Four cables, nineteen strands each.
Then suspenders and diagonal stays hung the deck from the cables and towers.
On May twenty fourth, eighteen eighty three, it opened. Emily crossed first. About a hundred fifty thousand people followed.
Trains crossed until nineteen forty four. Since twenty twenty one, it even has a protected bike lane.
Congrats! You've discovered how the Brooklyn Bridge was built.
